quotes.text: Use Radar to evaluate your payments regardless of payment processor.
Use the form below to request access to the Payment Evaluation API or additional capabilities, including raw card details, masked card details, and direct client signals.
Any `PaymentEvaluation` created with these parameters instead of a `PaymentMethod` returns only the `fraudulent_payment` signal.
Stripe returns a response with the `recommended_action` property and the `signals` object.
You can’t use a `PaymentEvaluation` that has already been associated with another payment.

source_assessments.reason: Add November’s expanded scope, separately approved inputs, response and confirmation boundaries while preserving dated May prerequisites and preview terms.

answers.Q1: The November capture of https://docs.stripe.com/radar/multiprocessor describes a business server requesting real-time Radar PaymentEvaluation risk signals for any processor, including Stripe, apart from actual processor execution. For non-Stripe payments, it documents a tokenized card PaymentMethod or approval-gated masked/raw card details, Radar Session or separately approved direct device details, and customer email. Raw card use is PCI DSS gated and masked input yields only fraudulent_payment. Stripe returns recommended_action and independently scored signals (new raw lines 39-77 and 79-133). If a separate evaluation precedes Stripe processing, default processing evaluates again and both are billed; the guide’s preview example specifies how eligible prior evaluations for the same payment can be reused at confirmation (new raw lines 135-150). May and source-stripe-radar-multiprocessor.md emphasize non-Stripe payments with a tokenized card, Radar Session and email (old raw lines 6-28).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/radar/multiprocessor, November substantively adds processor breadth, access requests, approved card and client-input alternatives, risk-response details, duplicate evaluation and billing scope, and separate Payment Records access (new raw lines 7-47, 121-150 and 152-162). Preserve the May non-Stripe scope and explicit private-preview labels for fraudulent_dispute and early_fraud_warning in source-stripe-radar-multiprocessor.md (old raw lines 6-28). November removes those heading labels and requires access, which does not establish general availability. Keep the exact risk-level boundary versus blocking-recommendation wording and its conflict with the adjacent transaction-risk guide. The expanded text diagram is illustrative, and the form link routes to an access request. Retain the reciprocal Radar concept, separate Radar Sessions/PAYG/Payment Records routes, and review of both dated captures (old raw lines 22-31; new raw lines 39-59 and 152-162).
